title: Henselization of pairs commutes with filtered colimits
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a directed set and $(A_\lambda,I_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ a directed system of pairs: commutative rings $A_\lambda$ with ideals $I_\lambda$ and ring maps $\varphi_{\mu\lambda}:A_\mu\to A_\lambda$ for $\mu\le\lambda$ (compatible, $\varphi_{\lambda\lambda}=\mathrm{id}$) with $\varphi_{\mu\lambda}(I_\mu)\subseteq I_\lambda$. Let $A=\varinjlim_\lambda A_\lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] with coprojections $\alpha_\lambda:A_\lambda\to A$, and let $I=\bigcup_\lambda\alpha_\lambda(I_\lambda)$ (an ideal of $A$, the colimit of the $I_\lambda$). For every $\lambda$ let $(A_\lambda^h,I_\lambda^h)$, $I_\lambda^h=I_\lambda A_\lambda^h$, be the henselization of $(A_\lambda,I_\lambda)$ [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization]. Then: (1) for $\mu\le\lambda$ there is exactly one ring map $\varphi^h_{\mu\lambda}:A_\mu^h\to A_\lambda^h$ with $\varphi^h_{\mu\lambda}\circ(A_\mu\to A_\mu^h)=(A_\lambda\to A_\lambda^h)\circ\varphi_{\mu\lambda}$, so that $(A^h_\lambda,I^h_\lambda)$ is a directed system of pairs; (2) $(\varinjlim_\lambda A^h_\lambda,\varinjlim_\lambda I^h_\lambda)$ is the henselization of $(A,I)$. In particular, if $(A,I)$ is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], then for every $\lambda$ there is exactly one ring map $\beta_\lambda:A_\lambda^h\to A$ with $\beta_\lambda\circ(A_\lambda\to A_\lambda^h)=\alpha_\lambda$; it maps $I_\lambda^h$ into $I$, the $\beta_\lambda$ are compatible with the $\varphi^h_{\mu\lambda}$, and they induce an isomorphism $\varinjlim_\lambda A_\lambda^h\cong A$ under which $\varinjlim_\lambda I^h_\lambda$ corresponds to $I$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A04 (lemma-henselization-colimit, line 3181) and its proof (Categories, adjoint-exact; Lemma 0FWT filtered-colimits-henselian; 'details omitted'); the functoriality (1), the uniqueness of $\beta_\lambda$ and $A^h=A$ for henselian $(A,I)$ are the left-adjoint property of Lemma Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization, line 2980: henselization is left adjoint to the inclusion of henselian pairs into pairs, the inclusion being fully faithful); used in this form in Fundamental Groups, proof of Lemma 0GS2 (pione.tex, General case: 'we see that $A=\colim A_i^h$')
